mAbs 2026-12-31 Medium

Beyond AlphaFold 3: a standardised benchmark of open-source co-folding models for antibody-antigen complexes, from docking accuracy to interaction specificity.

This study benchmarks five open-source co-folding models (AlphaFold 3, Protenix-v2, ESMFold2, ESMFold2-fast, and OpenDDE) on antibody-antigen complex prediction using a newly curated dataset of 200 complexes (SAbDab2-Bench) plus a reconstructed FoldBench subset (Ab-FoldBench). It evaluates docking accuracy and interaction specificity under standardized inputs, sampling, and interface metrics, providing the first head-to-head comparison of the latest generation of co-folding models for this therapeutically important problem.

Journal of immunotoxicology 2026-12-01 Medium

Impaired IFN-γ/STAT1-associated immune regulation contributes to 4-nonylphenol-aggravated allergic rhinitis.

This study integrates human transcriptomics, network toxicology, single-cell analysis, and molecular modeling to show that the endocrine-disrupting chemical 4-nonylphenol worsens allergic rhinitis by impairing IFN-γ/STAT1-associated immune regulation. Key genes IFNG and SKIL were downregulated in AR patients while CDKN1A was upregulated, with IFNG expression concentrated in T-cells. The findings suggest a mechanistic link between environmental chemical exposure and allergic disease via disrupted immune signaling.

Why Computational Predictions Fall Short in Subclass B1 Metallo-β-Lactamase Inhibitor Discovery: Progress, Pitfalls, and Translational Opportunities.

This review examines why computational methods for discovering subclass B1 metallo-β-lactamase inhibitors (targeting NDM-1, VIM-2, IMP-1) have produced many predicted binders that fail to translate into effective inhibitors. It catalogs the progress and pitfalls of computational screening approaches and highlights opportunities to improve translation from prediction to clinical candidates, given that no MBL inhibitors are currently approved for clinical use.

In silico antigenic and vaccinological characterization of two production-optimized recombinant yellow fever virus envelope proteins.

This study uses computational (in silico) methods to characterize two recombinant yellow fever virus envelope proteins derived from the Asibi and 17D strains, assessing their physicochemical properties, antigenicity, solubility, allergenicity, epitope conservation, and structural features. Through structural modeling, molecular docking, molecular dynamics, and immune simulation, the authors evaluate these proteins as potential nonreplicating vaccine candidates for populations where the live-attenuated 17D vaccine is restricted.

Fast and Slow Motions Drive Elusive Polymorphic Transitions in a Naphthalene-Diimide Crystal.

This study uses atomistic molecular dynamics simulations to investigate how a naphthalene-diimide organic semiconductor crystal transitions between two polymorphs (α at room temperature, γ at higher temperatures). The simulations reproduce both stable phases and refine unit-cell parameters and side-chain conformations that were only partially resolved experimentally, showing the α-to-γ transition proceeds through a sequential, nonconcerted mechanism involving fast and slow molecular motions.

Molecular Dynamics-Informed Prediction of Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS) Partitioning into Phospholipid Bilayer Environments.

This study uses molecular dynamics simulations to compute potential of mean force (PMF) curves that predict how diverse PFAS compounds partition into phospholipid bilayers. By integrating interaction energies along defined pathways, the approach offers a physics-based way to estimate membrane partitioning for PFAS with varied headgroups and fluorinated tails, which is otherwise difficult given their chemical diversity. The work provides a computational framework for linking PFAS structure to membrane accumulation relevant to cellular toxicity.

AlphaFold-based structural analysis of the Treponema pallidum proteome provides a clearer prediction of the organism's biological and pathogenic attributes.

The authors used AlphaFold protein structure prediction combined with FoldSeek structural matching to build a whole-proteome structural atlas of the syphilis pathogen Treponema pallidum Nichols strain. This approach allowed them to assign likely functions to previously uncharacterized proteins that lack sequence similarity to known proteins, providing new insights into the organism's biology and pathogenic mechanisms.

Machine Learning with Iterative Error-Driven Refinement for Predicting PFAS-Coated Surface Wettability.

This paper develops a machine learning-driven molecular dynamics simulation framework to predict the water and oil wettability of PFAS coatings on nylon, using iterative error-driven refinement to improve predictions. The approach aims to rationalize how molecular structure and surface organization govern intrinsic wettability, supporting the design of sustainable PFAS alternatives.

ACS materials Au 2026-11-11 Medium

Molecular Dynamics Simulations of Graphene and Graphene-Derived Ionic Liquid Supercapacitors: A Review of Methods and Applications.

This review surveys molecular dynamics simulation methods for modeling graphene and graphene-derived ionic liquid supercapacitors, focusing on how electrode-charging approaches (fixed-charge, constant-potential, and electronic-structure-aware methods) capture interfacial structure and capacitance. It argues that molecular-scale simulations are essential because neither continuum theory nor experiment alone resolves the relevant length and time scales governing capacitance. The review serves as a methodological guide for computational studies of graphene-based energy storage interfaces.

Strong light-matter coupling as a photonic substituent: cavity-induced electronic and structural control of regioselectivity in nitrobenzene.

This paper revisits a theoretical prediction that strong light-matter coupling in optical cavities can invert the regioselectivity of electrophilic aromatic substitution in nitrobenzene. Using correlated ab initio cavity QED methods (QED-DFT geometry relaxations plus QED-CCSD(2,2) calculations on Wheland intermediates), the authors confirm substantial energetic reordering, supporting the idea of a 'photonic substituent effect' on ground-state reactivity.

Discovery of novel small-molecule binders targeting IL-6 receptor conformational ensembles to regulate IL-6 signaling.

The work addresses the challenge of drugging the large protein–protein interaction interface between IL-6 and IL-6R, aiming to provide orally available alternatives to monoclonal antibodies for inflammation and immune-related diseases.

The information content of ultrafast observables: spectroscopy and scattering in excited norbornadiene.

This study evaluates how well different time-resolved spectroscopy and scattering techniques can distinguish between competing computational models of an ultrafast photochemical reaction—the photoisomerization of norbornadiene. By simulating photoelectron spectra and electron/X-ray scattering signals from four different electronic structure methods, the authors show which observables are most sensitive to the underlying nonadiabatic dynamics and can discriminate between models with different lifetimes and branching ratios.

Integrating Ion Mobility Mass Spectrometry Data with AlphaFold and Rosetta Improves Protein Complex Structure Prediction.

This paper presents a method that combines ion mobility mass spectrometry (IM-MS) collision cross section data with AlphaFold-predicted subunit structures and Rosetta docking to improve protein complex structure prediction. A new scoring function selects docked models that best agree with the experimental IM-MS data, addressing AlphaFold's limitations in modeling complexes.

LipidMem-BigSMILES (LiMBS): A Standardized Representation Language for Lipid Membrane Systems.

LiMBS is a new standardized line notation, extending SMILES and BigSMILES, to represent lipid membrane systems in a machine-readable format. It aims to solve the fragmentation of membrane descriptions across software-specific input files, improving reproducibility, data sharing, and enabling AI-driven analyses of molecular dynamics simulations.

Uncertainty Quantification for Free Energy Calculations by Generalized Hierarchical Bayesian Inference.

This paper introduces a generalized hierarchical Bayesian inference method for quantifying uncertainty in free energy calculations, addressing limitations of current Gaussian process approaches that often fail to properly account for hierarchical structure in simulation data. The method aims to provide more reliable uncertainty estimates, helping distinguish true physical features from artifacts due to limited sampling. This improves trustworthiness of free energy predictions from molecular dynamics simulations.

Chemical science 2026-11-06 Medium

Azobenzene-mediated reversible conformational switching in 9,9'-bifluorenylidene-based molecular machines.

The authors designed a molecular machine (Azo-BF-Azo) that combines a flexible 9,9'-bifluorenylidene core with two photoswitchable azobenzene units, allowing visible light to drive reversible changes in the molecule's shape. Using NMR, UV-vis spectroscopy, and computations, they show that 525 nm irradiation triggers azobenzene switching that in turn controls the conformation of the BF core. This demonstrates external light-based control of conformational motion in an intrinsically dynamic molecule.

Characterization of Clonixeril as a Positive Modulator of DMXAA-Induced Murine STING Signaling.

Clonixeril (CXL), previously identified as an inhibitor of human STING signaling, was tested against murine STING and found instead to positively modulate DMXAA-induced mSTING activation. This species-specific divergence highlights functional differences between mouse and human STING despite structural conservation, with implications for interpreting mouse-model studies of STING-targeted therapeutics.

Novel EGCG Analog Modulates Host Immune Response to Promote Intracellular Clearance of Staphylococcus Aureus Through Interaction With the 67-kDa Laminin Receptor.

This study investigates how EGCG, a green tea polyphenol, and its synthetic analogs (MCC-2 and MCC-4) modulate the host immune response to clear intracellular Staphylococcus aureus, a major cause of persistent bacteremia. The authors identify the 67-kDa laminin receptor (67LR) as a putative target mediating these immunometabolic effects in liver macrophages. The work suggests that EGCG analogs could be developed as host-directed therapeutics against SAB.

PLoS computational biology 2026-11-01 Medium

Handshake: Partner-specific protein-protein binding site prediction at scale using ProstT5 and cross-chain attention.

HandShake is a sequence-only computational tool that predicts which residues of a protein form the binding interface with a specific partner, without requiring 3D structural data at test time. It combines the ProstT5 protein language model with cross-chain attention to capture partner-specific interactions, addressing limitations of prior methods such as small training datasets and inconsistent redundancy filtering. The approach enables partner-specific binding site prediction at scale, with implications for drug discovery and protein function annotation.

Targeting TLR2 to Overcome Autophagy-Dependent Chemoresistance in Gastric Cancer: Integrating Molecular Docking, Mechanistic Validation, and Therapeutic Evaluation.

This study used computational drug repurposing to identify FDA-approved compounds that inhibit TLR2, a receptor implicated in autophagy-driven chemoresistance in gastric cancer. Nilotinib and Lomitapide emerged from virtual screening of 1,555 drugs and were experimentally validated to overcome autophagy-dependent resistance in gastric adenocarcinoma cells. The work links TLR2 signaling to chemoresistance and proposes repurposed drugs as combination therapeutic candidates.

Small science 2026-11-01 Medium

Void-Assisted Extrinsic Charge Trapping Governs Hole Transport in Organic Semiconductors.

This study investigates how extrinsic trap states form in single-layer organic semiconductor devices, which are used to suppress efficiency rolloff in electrically pumped organic lasers. By combining current-voltage measurements of hole-only devices with molecular dynamics simulations of BZ derivatives, the authors identify void-assisted extrinsic charge trapping as the dominant factor governing hole transport. The work clarifies how structural voids in the organic film create trap states that promote nonradiative recombination and reduce electroluminescence efficiency.

Computational Discovery of Plant-Derived Peptides with Therapeutic Potential: A Scoping Review.

This scoping review maps the literature on computational discovery of plant-derived peptides with therapeutic potential, screening over 5,000 records and charting 79 sources published between 2021 and 2026. It finds that most work consists of primary studies, with a smaller share describing tools or databases, and highlights gaps in reporting practice across the field. The review provides a structured overview of methods, scope, and evidence quality in this emerging area.

N-glycoproteomic profiling reveals aberrant ITGB1 glycosylation in hyperoxia-induced bronchopulmonary dysplasia.

This study used N-glycoproteomic profiling in a mouse model of hyperoxia-induced bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) to map changes in protein glycosylation. The authors identified aberrant N-glycosylation of integrin beta-1 (ITGB1), suggesting that altered ECM-receptor glycosylation may contribute to arrested alveolarization in preterm lung disease. The work provides a first glycoproteomic landscape for BPD and nominates ITGB1 glycosylation as a candidate pathogenic mechanism.
